name: Adam Weishaupt
description: Bavarian canon-law professor who founded the Illuminati in 1776 and spent his exile watching European reactionaries transform his defunct debating society into history's favourite hidden hand.

name: Lee Harvey Oswald
description: Ex-Marine defector to the USSR identified as Kennedy's assassin by both official investigations. His murder by Jack Ruby before trial — and his declaration 'I'm just a patsy' — made him the permanently unresolved centre of the case.

name: J. Edgar Hoover
description: FBI director for 48 years who ran COINTELPRO, kept secret files on politicians and public figures, and personally targeted Martin Luther King Jr. The documented reality of his abuses anchors the plausibility of surveillance-state theories generally.

name: Bob Lazar
description: Claimed in 1989 to have reverse-engineered alien propulsion at 'S-4' near Area 51, introducing 'element 115' to UFO lore. His stated MIT/Caltech credentials have never been verified; supporters cite his description of the classified base's features. The most influential single witness in UFO conspiracy culture.

name: Alex Jones
description: Broadcaster whose InfoWars built the commercial template of conspiracy media — from Bohemian Grove infiltration (2000) to Sandy Hook denial, for which juries awarded ~$1.5 billion in defamation damages. Central case study in the monetization of conspiracy narratives.

name: David Icke
description: Former footballer and broadcaster turned author of a vast cosmology in which reptilian entities manipulate humanity. His work exemplifies the 'superconspiracy' genre and the migration of New Age audiences toward conspiracy belief.

name: Edward Snowden
description: NSA contractor whose 2013 disclosures documented global mass surveillance. Whether framed as whistleblower or defector, his leak is the modern reference point for the difference between evidenced revelation and speculation.

name: Jim Garrison
description: New Orleans DA who brought the only JFK-assassination prosecution (Clay Shaw, acquitted in under an hour in 1969). His investigation — dramatized in Oliver Stone's JFK — institutionalized the case's conspiracy tradition, and drew criticism for its methods.

name: Mark Lane
description: Attorney whose Rush to Judgment (1966) was the first bestselling critique of the Warren Report, effectively founding assassination research as a public genre — and later defending the Peoples Temple shortly before Jonestown.

name: Serge Monast
description: Québécois journalist who originated Project Blue Beam (1994), the holographic false-rapture theory. His death of heart attack two years later is itself folded into the theory — a compact example of self-sealing narrative.

name: Bill Kaysing
description: Former Rocketdyne technical writer whose 'We Never Went to the Moon' (1976) founded moon-hoax literature, establishing arguments (waving flag, missing stars, radiation) recycled ever since despite repeated refutation.

name: Heribert Illig
description: German author of the Phantom Time Hypothesis, arguing three medieval centuries were invented. His systematic (if refuted) argument makes him the standard citation in chronological-revisionism debates.
